the_one_ring.description: The One Ring is the ultimate artifact of power in the Arda galaxy, forged by Sauron in the fires of Orodruin (Mount Doom). It contains a great portion of Sauron's own power and was designed to dominate all other Rings of Power and control their bearers. In the galaxy, it is a device that can command all other Ring artifacts and exert influence across light-years.

light_use.description: The Ring cannot be used for good. Even those with pure intentions are gradually corrupted by its influence. The only safe course is to resist its temptation and ultimately destroy it.
principles: The Ring must not be used, even for seemingly noble purposes
Resist the temptation to wield power over others
Trust in small acts of courage rather than grand displays of power
The Ring can only be unmade in the fires where it was forged

dark_use.description: The Ring amplifies the wearer's desire for power and domination. It grants invisibility, extended life, and the ability to command those who wear lesser Rings, but at the cost of the wearer's soul.
effects: Invisibility — shifts the wearer to the Wraith-world
Extended lifespan — halts aging but does not grant true life
Domination — commands bearers of the Nine Rings (Nazgûl) and Seven Rings
Corruption — gradually erodes the wearer's moral compass
Connection to Sauron — the Ring desires to return to its master

inscription.text: Ash nazg durbatulûk, ash nazg gimbatul, ash nazg thrakatulûk agh burzum-ishi krimpatul.
inscription.translation: One Ring to rule them all, One Ring to find them, One Ring to bring them all and in the darkness bind them.

the_three_elven_rings.description: The Three Elven Rings were forged by Celebrimbor without Sauron's direct touch, though Sauron's knowledge of ring-making gave him inherent power over them. They were hidden from Sauron and serve to preserve, heal, and protect.

rings.name: Narya
rings.description: The Ring of Fire. It rekindles the hearts of the free and inspires hope and courage in times of despair.
rings.galaxy_function: An energy weapon or power source that can ignite star-drives and inspire fleets

rings.name: Nenya
rings.description: The Ring of Water, also called the Ring of Truth. It preserves and protects, maintaining Lothlórien's timeless beauty.
rings.galaxy_function: A shield or preservation device that can protect entire systems from decay and corruption

rings.name: Vilya
rings.description: The most powerful of the Three. It enhances the wearer's inherent abilities and maintains Rivendell as a refuge.
rings.galaxy_function: A command device that amplifies the wielder's abilities and maintains safe zones in the galaxy

eras.description: The history of Arda is divided into Ages, each marked by great events and the rise and fall of powers.

ages.name: The Music of the Ainur
ages.description: Eru Ilúvatar created the Ainur (Holy Ones) and set them to singing the Music of the Ainur, which envisioned all of creation. This theme became the blueprint for Eä, the universe.
key_events: The Music of the Ainur — the thematic vision of all creation
Melkor's discord — the first introduction of opposition and chaos
Ilúvatar's second theme — 'Behold! I will make powers anew ye deem not mighty or born, but they shall rise'

ages.name: The Beginning of Days
ages.description: Eä was made manifest. The Ainur entered the universe, and the Valar (Powers of Arda) began shaping the world. The Two Trees grew in Valinor, illuminating the Undying Lands.
key_events: Creation of Eä (the universe) and Arda (the world)
The Valar enter Arda and begin shaping it
Growth of the Two Trees: Telperion (Silver) and Laurelin (Gold)
Melkor's destruction of the Two Trees
Creation of the Sun (Anar) and Moon (Isil) from the last fruits of the Trees

ages.name: First Age
ages.description: The Age of the Elves. The Noldor returned to Middle-earth in exile, waging war against Morgoth (Melkor). The Silmarils were stolen and eventually recovered at great cost.
key_events: The Kinslaying at Alqualondë
Dagor-nuin-Giliath (Battle under the Stars)
Fall of Nogrod and Belegost
Battle of Unnumbered Years begins
Birth of Fëanor's sons and the Oath of Fëanor
Dagor Bragollach (Battle of Sudden Flame)
Nírnaeth Arnoediad (Battle of Unleashed Tears)
Hading of Hithlum
Battle of the Thousand Trees
Sack of Nogrod
Death of Húrin and captivity of Hurin
Túrin's tragedy in Doriath
Battle of Lammoth
Fall of Gondolin
Death of Túrin Turambar
Fall of Nargothrond
Death of Eärendil's father, Turgon
Dagor Dagorath prophesied
War of Wrath — Eärendil brings the Host of the Valar; Morgoth is defeated and cast into the Void

ages.name: Second Age
ages.description: The Age of Men and the rise of Sauron. The Elves and Men of Númenor became great powers. Sauron deceived the Elves into forging the Rings of Power, leading to the Last Alliance and the first casting of the One Ring.
key_events: Rising of the Sun and Moon
Awakening of the Elves at Cuiviénen
Coming of the Valar and building of Valinor
Gift of the Valar: Immortality for Elves
Awakening of Men in Hildórien
Founding of Númenor as gift to faithful Men
Sauron's rise in Middle-earth
Creation of the Rings of Power: Three, Seven, and Nine
Sauron reveals himself and claims the One Ring
First Age of Númenórean power and exploration
Ar-Pharazôn's golden age and subsequent pride
Sauron captured by Ar-Pharazôn
Sauron corrupts the Númenóreans
Akallabêth — Downfall of Númenor: the land is sunk into the sea
Last Alliance of Elves and Men marches on Mordor
Battle of Dagorlad
Siege of Barad-dûr
Duel of Elendil and Sauron; Elendil falls
Isildur cuts the Ring from Sauron's hand; Sauron's spirit is defeated
Isildur takes the Ring and spares it
Founding of Arnor and Gondor
Gladden Fields massacre; the Ring is lost in the Anduin

ages.name: Third Age
ages.description: The Age when the Shadow returned. The Ring lay hidden for millennia, then resurfaced to become the instrument of the War of the Ring. Sauron was finally defeated when the Ring was destroyed.
key_events: The Ring lies hidden in the River Anduin
Sméagol finds the Ring; becomes Gollum
War of the Elves and Sauron
Last Glorious Expedition of the Númenórean kings
Balrog awakens in Moria
The White Council discovers Sauron in Dol Guldur
Saruman drives Sauron from Dol Guldur; begins his own quest for the Ring
The Watchful Peace — Sauron lies hidden while rebuilding
Gandalf discovers the Eye; Saruman betrays the White Council
Gandalf sent to the Shire to search for the Ring
Bilbo finds the Ring has powers; Gandalf confirms it is the One Ring
Frodo inherits the Ring
Council of Elrond — the Fellowship is formed
The Fellowship of the Ring is broken at Moria
Faramir and Frodo in Ithilien
Shelob's Lair and Cirith Ungol
Faramir releases Frodo and Sam
Sam sees the stars above the clouds — hope renewed
Frodo and Sam enter Mordor
Capture by Orcs; Shelob kills Frodo (temporarily)
Sam takes the Ring; 'I will take the Ring, Mr. Frodo'
Scouring of the Shire (after the main events)
Battle of the Pelennor Fields
Riders of Rohan arrive at the Hornburg
Battle of the Hornburg (Helms Deep)
Treebeard and the Ents march on Isengard
Frodo reaches Mount Doom; the Ring is destroyed
Sauron is defeated; the Fourth Age begins
The Grey Havens — the Ring-bearers depart for Valinor

ages.name: Fourth Age
ages.description: The Age of Men begins. The Elves fade from the world, sailing West to Valinor. Aragorn rules as King Elessar, and the galaxy enters a new era of peace under human stewardship.
key_events: Coronation of Aragorn and Arwen
The Elves begin departing for Valinor
The galaxy enters a long peace
The Dwarves rebuild Moria
The Hobbits flourish in the Shire
Aragorn dies after 120 years; the Ring-bearers have already departed

realms.name: Rivendell (Imladris)
realms.description: A hidden star system protected by spatial distortions and elven wards. An archive of ancient knowledge and a diplomatic center for the Free Peoples. Founded by Elrond after the First Age.
notable_features: The Last Homely House — a waystation for travelers
Ancient archives containing knowledge from the First Age
Protected by the Ring Vilya and elven enchantments
Spatial distortions make it difficult for enemies to find

realms.name: Lothlórien
realms.description: A star system bathed in golden light where time flows differently. The Trees of Lothlórien echo the Two Trees of Valinor. A place of healing, wisdom, and preservation.
notable_features: Time flows differently — days feel like hours
The Mallorn trees — golden, luminous, and ancient
Galadriel's Mirror — can see past, present, and possible futures
Lambengolîr — the Silver Lake
Protected by Nenya; preserves the realm from decay

realms.name: Gondor
realms.description: A powerful, centralized star empire descended from Númenor. Known for white towers, advanced palantír communication technology, and a proud martial tradition. The central human power in the galaxy.
realms.capital: Minas Tirith — a great fortress world
notable_features: The White Tree — symbol of the realm
Palantír network — instant communication across light-years
The White Tower of Orthanc (shared with Isengard)
Ancient fortifications and star-fortresses
Descendants of the Dúnedain — long-lived and wise

realms.name: Rohan
realms.description: A system of open plains and grasslands inhabited by the Éothéod, allies of Gondor. Known for fast ships, cavalry culture, and fierce warriors who ride into battle with song and horn.
notable_features: The Éothéod — master riders and pilots
Helm's Deep — an impregnable fortress station
Meduseld — the Golden Hall
Alliance with Gondor through the Oath of Eorl
Fast transit ships and cavalry tactics

realms.name: Mordor
realms.description: A scorched star system dominated by a red star. The industrial war machine of Sauron, where orcs are mass-produced and war machines are forged. The central evil power in the galaxy.
realms.capital: Barad-dûr — a dark fortress station orbiting a lava world
notable_features: Orodruin (Mount Doom) — a volcanic star where the One Ring was forged
Barad-dûr — the Dark Tower, Sauron's seat of power
The Eye of Sauron — an all-seeing surveillance system
Black Gates of Morannon — the main defensive line
Mines and forges producing endless armies
The Palantír of Cirith Ungor — used by Sauron to deceive enemies

realms.name: Isengard
realms.description: A world stripped of nature, converted into a massive factory complex. Saruman the White, once chief of the Istari, corrupted by the desire for the Ring, now produces war machines and Uruk-hai.
realms.capital: Orthanc — an ancient tower of Adûnaic stone
notable_features: Orthanc — an indestructible tower, one of the seven Palantíri
Massive factories and war machine production
Uruk-hai breeding programs
The Hornburg (Helm's Deep) — nearby fortress, later captured
Tree-cutting and environmental destruction
The Palantír of Orthanc — used by Saruman to communicate with Sauron

realms.name: The Shire
realms.description: A quiet, green star system on the galactic fringe — overlooked by major powers but strategically located. Home to the Hobbits, small but resilient colonists who value peace, food, and comfort above all.
notable_features: Bag End — the home of the Ring-bearer
The Party Field — celebration grounds
Overlooked by major powers due to its unassuming nature
Rich agricultural output despite small size
The Scouring — later invaded by Saruman's forces

realms.name: Moria (Khazad-dûm)
realms.description: A hollowed-out planet or asteroid belt with vast underground forges. Once the greatest dwarf kingdom, now haunted by a Balrog. Rich in mithril, a rare and powerful metal.
realms.ruler: Formerly King Durin's line; now abandoned
notable_features: The Kibil-nála and Narvi — great waterfalls
Seven halls of Durin — vast underground chambers
Mithril mines — the most valuable resource in the galaxy
The Balrog — an ancient demon of fire and shadow
The Bridge of Khazad-dûm — a key defensive position

realms.name: Númenor (Elenna)
realms.description: A once-great star system that was destroyed when it was sunk into a black hole by Eru Ilúvatar. Its ruins are legendary, and its descendants founded Gondor and Arnor.
realms.ruler: Formerly the Kings of Númenor; now lost
notable_features: Meneltarma — the Hill of the Faithful, a sacred site
The Star of Elenna — a great beacon
Sunk into the sea (black hole) by Ilúvatar himself
The Straight Road — a path that still leads to Valinor
Legacy: the Dúnedain (Rangers of the North and South)

realms.name: Harad
realms.description: Hot, tropical star systems with unique flora and fauna. Trade partners or rivals of Gondor, with diverse cultures and war elephants (Mûmakil).
notable_features: Mûmakil — giant war beasts used in combat
Rich trade routes and exotic resources
Allied with Mordor during the War of the Ring
Diverse cultures and languages
White Hand — a cult devoted to Sauron

realms.name: Rhûn
realms.description: Vast, open star systems on the eastern rim of the galaxy. Nomadic and warlike peoples, often drawn into Sauron's service.
notable_features: The Easterlings — diverse nomadic cultures
The Útúlië — a faction that allied with Gondor
Vast open systems suitable for cavalry tactics
Often manipulated by Sauron through the Palantíri
The Ashen Mouths of Mazar — gateway to Mordor

realms.name: Forodwaith
realms.description: Frozen star systems at the galactic pole. Dangerous and sparsely populated, with the northern lights (aurora) visible. Home to ancient cold and the remnants of Angmar.
notable_features: The Ice-crown (Himring) — a frozen mountain range
Remnants of the Witch-king's former power
Ancient cold that even the Valar feared
The aurora — spiritual lights visible from these systems
Arnor's northern remnants — the Fellowship of the Ring

realms.name: Mirkwood
realms.description: A star system shrouded in dark energy or nebula, dangerous to navigate. Once the beautiful Eryn Vorn, now corrupted by shadow. Home to giant spiders and Wood-elves.
notable_features: The Great Forest — shrouded in darkness
Giant spiders descended from Ungoliant
The Wood-elves — isolated and proud
The River Running — a boundary between Mirkwood and the Wild
Dol Guldur — Sauron's hidden fortress (later revealed)

realms.name: Fangorn
realms.description: A living star system where the trees themselves are sentient (Ents). The oldest and most mysterious of the Free Peoples' strongholds.
notable_features: The Ents — ancient tree-shepherds, slow to anger but devastating
Living trees that can walk and fight
Entwives — lost, seeking them is the Ents' greatest sorrow
The Entwash — a great river
Critical to the destruction of Isengard

species.name: Elves (Quendi)
species.description: The Firstborn of Ilúvatar. Immortal, attuned to the stars, and fading from the galaxy. They are the most wise and beautiful of all peoples, with deep knowledge of craft, song, and magic.
traits: Immortality — bound to Arda until its end
Keen senses — superior sight, hearing, and perception
Attuned to the stars — deep connection to Varda's light
Fading — gradually becoming invisible to those without elven blood
Choice — may choose to sail to Valinor or remain in Middle-earth

subtypes.name: Noldor
subtypes.description: The Crafty; master smiths and scholars; exiled from Valinor

subtypes.name: Teleri
subtypes.description: The Last; include the Wood-elves and those who sailed to Valinor

subtypes.name: Vanyar
subtypes.description: The Fair; most loyal to the Valar; few remain in Middle-earth

species.galaxy_role: Ancient diplomats, scholars, and guardians of knowledge

species.name: Men (Atani)
species.description: The Secondborn of Ilúvatar. Mortal but ambitious, gifted with the Gift of Ilúvatar — the ability to depart the world entirely. They are the inheritors of Arda and the builders of great empires.
traits: Mortality — the Gift of Ilúvatar; death is not a curse but a gift
Ambition — driven to explore, build, and conquer
Variety — diverse cultures, languages, and abilities
Susceptibility to corruption — more easily influenced by the Ring
Potential for greatness — capable of both great heroism and great evil

subtypes.name: Dúnedain
subtypes.description: Men of the West; long-lived, wise, descendants of Númenor

subtypes.name: Éothéod
subtypes.description: The horse-lords of Rohan; fierce warriors and riders

subtypes.name: Haradrim
subtypes.description: Southern peoples; diverse cultures and traditions

subtypes.name: Easterlings
subtypes.description: Eastern peoples; nomadic and warlike

species.galaxy_role: Rising power; explorers, builders, and inheritors of the galaxy

species.name: Dwarves (Khazad)
species.description: Created by Aulë the Smith, adopted by Ilúvatar. Master engineers and miners, stubborn and resilient. They excel at underground and asteroid operations, and are renowned for their craftsmanship.
traits: Master craftsmen — unparalleled skill in metalwork and stonework
Stubbornness — will not yield easily in conflict or negotiation
Resilience — can endure harsh conditions and long journeys
Treasure-lust — strong desire for gold, gems, and mithril
Long-lived — though mortal, they live much longer than most Men

subtypes.name: Durin's Folk
subtypes.description: The longest-lived and most noble; of Moria and Erebor

subtypes.name: Fire-beards
subtypes.description: Red-bearded dwarves of the Iron Hills

subtypes.name: Broad-beams
subtypes.description: Dwarves of the Grey Mountains

species.name: Hobbits (Halflings)
species.description: A small, unassuming people related to Men. Overlooked by major powers, they are surprisingly tough, resilient, and resistant to the Ring's corruption. Their simplicity is their strength.
traits: Small stature — easily overlooked, which is a tactical advantage
Resilience — tougher than they appear; can endure great hardship
Resistance to corruption — the Ring's power over them is weaker
Love of comfort — food, pipe-weed, and peaceful living
Unexpected courage — when pushed, they show remarkable bravery

subtypes.name: Hobbits of the Shire
subtypes.description: The main population; peaceful and agrarian

subtypes.name: Harfoots
subtypes.description: Brown-haired, love hills; the majority of Shire hobbits

subtypes.name: Stoors
subtypes.description: Tanner-skinned, love water; live near rivers

subtypes.name: Fallohides
subtypes.description: Fair-haired, taller; descended from northern stock

species.galaxy_role: Unassuming but resilient colonists; the unlikely saviors of the galaxy

species.name: Ents (Shepherds of the Trees)
species.description: Ancient, tree-like beings created by Eru Ilúvatar at the request of the Valar. The oldest living beings in Middle-earth, slow to act but devastating when roused to anger.
traits: Extreme longevity — some are older than any other living being
Slow deliberation — take great time to decide on action
Immense strength — can uproot trees and destroy fortifications
Connection to nature — can communicate with trees
Devastating wrath — when roused, they are unstoppable
species.galaxy_role: Ancient guardians of forest worlds; last resort against industrial destruction

species.name: Orcs
species.description: Corrupted beings created by Morgoth, possibly from tortured Elves. Mass-produced soldiers of Mordor and Isengard, serving Sauron and his allies. They are the primary infantry of the Forces of Darkness.
traits: Mass-produced — bred and raised in vast numbers
Hatred of light — especially sunlight and elven light
Cruelty — enjoy torture and destruction
Discipline — can be organized into effective military units
Variety — many subtypes with different abilities

subtypes.name: Uruk-hai
subtypes.description: Larger, stronger orcs bred by Saruman; can endure sunlight

subtypes.name: Olog-hai
subtypes.description: Troll-blooded orcs; even larger and more powerful

subtypes.name: Goblin
subtypes.description: Smaller orcs of the mountains and mines

species.galaxy_role: War machines of Mordor; the primary enemy infantry

species.name: Maiar
species.description: Powerful spiritual beings, lesser than the Valar but greater than all other creatures. Include the Wizards (Istari), Balrogs, and nature spirits. They are the servants of the Valar.
traits: Immense power — far beyond Elves and Men
Spiritual nature — can take physical form at will
Ancient — existed before the world was made
Restricted — the Istari are bound in mortal bodies
Diverse — range from benevolent (Gandalf) to evil (Balrogs)

subtypes.name: Istari (Wizards)
subtypes.description: Five Maiar sent to aid the Free Peoples; Gandalf, Saruman, Radagast, and the Blue Wizards

subtypes.name: Balrogs
subtypes.description: Fallen Maiar of fire; demons of shadow and flame

subtypes.name: Nature spirits
subtypes.description: Melian, Eönwë, and other benevolent spirits

species.galaxy_role: Powerful spiritual beings; advisors, warriors, and ancient forces

key_events.name: Council of Elrond
key_events.description: The great council held at Rivendell to decide the fate of the One Ring. Representatives of all Free Peoples gathered, and the Fellowship of the Ring was formed.
key_events.outcome: The Fellowship of the Ring was formed to carry the Ring to Mount Doom

key_events.name: Fall of the Fellowship at Moria
key_events.description: The Fellowship was attacked by a Balrog in the mines of Moria. Gandalf fell with the Balrog into the abyss, and the Fellowship was broken.
key_events.outcome: Gandalf fell; the Fellowship was broken; Frodo chose to go to Mordor alone

key_events.name: Battle of the Hornburg (Helm's Deep)
key_events.description: The greatest battle of Rohan. Saruman's forces attacked Helm's Deep, but the Riders of Rohan, aided by Éomer's riders and an avalanche, won a decisive victory.
key_events.outcome: Decisive victory for Rohan; Saruman's army destroyed

key_events.name: Battle of the Pelennor Fields
key_events.description: The largest battle in the War of the Ring. Mordor's forces besieged Minas Tirith, but the Riders of Rohan arrived at dawn, turning the tide. Éowyn killed the Witch-king.
key_events.outcome: Victory for the Free Peoples; the Witch-king was slain; Faramir wounded; Théoden died

key_events.name: Destruction of the One Ring
key_events.description: Frodo and Sam reached Mount Doom. Though Frodo claimed the Ring at the last moment, it was cast into the fires by Gollum, who fell while biting it from Frodo's finger.
key_events.outcome: Sauron was defeated; the Ring was destroyed; the Fourth Age began

key_events.name: Downfall of Númenor (Akallabêth)
key_events.description: Ar-Pharazôn sailed against Valinor, and Eru Ilúvatar sank Númenor into the sea. The world was remade, and the Undying Lands were removed from the circles of the world.
key_events.outcome: Númenor was destroyed; the world was remade; the Undying Lands were hidden

key_events.name: War of Wrath
key_events.description: Eärendil brought the Host of the Valar to Middle-earth. Morgoth was defeated, his forces destroyed, and he was cast into the Void beyond the world.
key_events.outcome: Morgoth was defeated; the Silmarils were lost (one to sea, one to earth, one to sky); the First Age ended

constellations.name: Valacirca (Durin's Crown)
constellations.description: The Lord's Chair — the most prominent constellation in the Arda galaxy, formed by seven stars arranged in a crown shape. It serves as the central navigation point and galactic hub. The Elven name means 'Chair of the Valar.'
constellations.galaxy_role: Central hub system; the seven stars form a trade nexus connecting all sectors
notable_features: The central star is the brightest in the galaxy
Used as the primary navigation reference by all factions
The crown shape is a symbol of elven authority
Dwarves call it the Seven Stars of Durin

constellations.name: Menelmacar (The Crowned Stars)
constellations.description: The Crowned Stars — a circular constellation representing the crown of Gil-galad, last High King of the Noldor. A symbol of elven kingship and the fading age of the Elves.
constellations.galaxy_role: Elven diplomatic zone; neutral territory governed by elven law
notable_features: Associated with the memory of Gil-galad
A neutral zone where elven law prevails
Contains ancient elven waystations

constellations.name: Remmirath (The Great Snake)
constellations.description: The Great Snake — a long, winding constellation that stretches across the galaxy. Named after Ungoliant, the great spider who devoured the light of the Two Trees. A dangerous region to navigate.
constellations.galaxy_role: Dangerous trade route; pirates and corsairs hide among its stars
notable_features: Named after Ungoliant, enemy of the Valar
Long and winding — easy to get lost in
Home to the Corsairs of Umbar and other pirates

constellations.name: Thelassiel (The Harp)
constellations.description: The Harp — a beautiful constellation shaped like a harp, associated with the music of the Ainur and the songs of the Elves. A peaceful region of the galaxy.
constellations.galaxy_role: Cultural and artistic center; elven music and song are preserved here
notable_features: Associated with the Music of the Ainur
A center of elven art and culture
The stars are said to sing when viewed from Valinor

constellations.name: Mornifel (The Naught-star)
constellations.description: The Naught-star — the star of doom and evil, associated with Morgoth's corruption. Also called the 'Star of Doom.' It marks the northern pole of the galaxy and is a symbol of despair.
constellations.galaxy_role: The northern pole; a dark and dangerous region influenced by Morgoth's legacy
notable_features: Associated with Morgoth's evil
Marks the northern pole of the galaxy
A symbol of despair and doom
The region around it is cold and hostile

constellations.name: Aldarion's Stars (The Ship)
constellations.description: Named after King Aldarion the Shipwright of Númenor, this constellation represents a great ship. It marks the Straight Road, the path that leads from the material world to Valinor.
constellations.galaxy_role: The Straight Road — a hidden hyperspace lane leading to Valinor
notable_features: Named after King Aldarion of Númenor
Marks the Straight Road to Valinor
Only those with elven blood can navigate it safely
The Grey Havens ships use this route

constellations.name: The Silmaril Star (Eärendil's Star)
constellations.description: The brightest star in the sky, bearing one of the three Silmarils. Eärendil the Mariner sails the heavens in his ship Vingilot, bearing the Silmaril as a beacon of hope. Visible across the entire galaxy.
constellations.galaxy_role: Galactic beacon of hope; visible from every system
notable_features: Contains one of the three Silmarils
Eärendil sails eternally, a sign of hope
Visible from every point in the galaxy
Its light can repel darkness and evil

valar_planets.name: Manwë's Realm
valar_planets.vala: Manwë Súlimo, King of the Arda
valar_planets.description: The highest planet in the galaxy, where Manwë sits upon his throne and hears the prayers of all free beings. A world of endless skies and storms.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: The highest authority; a world of judgment and prayer
notable_features: Taniquetil — the highest peak, visible from all worlds
Manwë's throne — from which he hears all prayers
Endless skies and storms
The winds of change blow from here

valar_planets.name: Varda's Realm
valar_planets.vala: Varda Elentári, Queen of the Stars
valar_planets.description: The realm of the Star-maiden, who kindled the stars. A world of brilliant light and navigation, where the constellations are most clearly visible.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: Navigation and astronomy center; the source of starlight
notable_features: Varda kindled the stars at the request of the Elves
The brightest point in the galaxy
Elves pray to Varda for guidance
The source of all starlight in the galaxy

valar_planets.name: Ulmo's Realm
valar_planets.description: The realm of Ulmo, who has no fixed dwelling but roams the waters of Arda. A world of oceans, rivers, and underground streams. He is closest to the children of Ilúvatar.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: Ocean world; controls all water in the galaxy
notable_features: Ulmo has no fixed throne — he roams the waters
Closest of the Valar to the children of Ilúvatar
Controls all water, rivers, and seas in the galaxy
Warned the Elves of Morgoth's schemes

valar_planets.name: Aulë's Realm
valar_planets.description: The realm of Aulë, creator of the Dwarves. A world of mountains, forges, and precious metals. The greatest craftsman among the Valar.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: Mining and manufacturing world; source of rare metals
notable_features: Aulë created the Dwarves (though Ilúvatar gave them life)
World of mountains, forges, and treasures
Source of mithril and other rare metals
Sauron was once Aulë's Maia

valar_planets.name: Yavanna's Realm
valar_planets.description: The realm of Yavanna, who created the Two Trees and all growing things. A world of endless forests, gardens, and fertility. Mother of Arda.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: Agricultural and biological world; source of life
notable_features: Yavanna created the Two Trees of Valinor
World of endless forests and gardens
Created the Ents to protect the trees
Mother of Arda; giver of all growing things

valar_planets.name: Mandos' Realm
valar_planets.description: The Halls of Mandos, where the spirits of the dead wait before reincarnation. A solemn and mysterious world where the fates of all beings are recorded.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: The afterworld; spirits wait here before passing on
notable_features: The Halls of Mandos — where spirits of the dead wait
The fates of all beings are recorded here
Mandos prophesied the doom of the Noldor
No one leaves the Halls unless Mandos wills it

valar_planets.name: Tilion's Realm
valar_planets.description: The realm of Tilion, who tends the Moon (Isil). A world of darkness and silver light, where the night is beautiful and mysterious.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: Night-side of the galaxy; moonlight and shadows
notable_features: Tilion tends the Moon, made from the last fruit of Telperion
World of darkness and silver light
Associated with night and mystery
Love of Yavanna — a secret romance among the Valar

valar_planets.name: Ainú's Realm
valar_planets.description: The realm of Nienna, who teaches wisdom through suffering. A world of healing, compassion, and understanding. Her tears formed the rivers of Valinor.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: Healing and wisdom world; a place of refuge
notable_features: Nienna teaches wisdom through suffering
Her tears formed the rivers of Valinor
A world of healing and compassion
Mandos and Irmo are her siblings

valar_planets.name: Irmo's Realm
valar_planets.description: The realm of Irmo, Lord of Dreams. A world of visions, prophecies, and the healing power of sleep. The Gardens of Irmo are a place of rest and renewal.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: Dream and vision world; source of prophecies
notable_features: Irmo is the Lord of Dreams and Visions
The Gardens of Irmo — a place of rest and renewal
Prophecies and visions originate here
Dreams can reveal truth or deceive

valar_planets.name: Melian's Realm
valar_planets.vala: Melian the Maia, Queen of Doriath
valar_planets.description: The realm of Melian, a Maia who became queen of Doriath and mother of Lúthien. Her Girdle (Maeglin's Girdle) was an enchantment that protected Doriath from all who sought to enter by force.
valar_planets.galaxy_role: Protected sanctuary; a hidden zone shielded by elven enchantments
notable_features: Melian's Girdle — an impenetrable enchantment
Mother of Lúthien Tinúviel
Wife of Thingol, King of Doriath
Her protection made Doriath inviolate

artifacts.name: The One Ring
artifacts.description: A device that can command all other Rings; grants immense power but corrupts the user. Forged by Sauron in the fires of Orodruin.

artifacts.name: The Palantíri
artifacts.description: Seven seeing-stones that allow instant communication across light-years. Controlled by Gondor, but some fell into enemy hands.

artifacts.name: The Silmarils
artifacts.description: Three jewels containing the light of the Two Trees — the most precious artifacts in the galaxy. One is in the sky (with Eärendil), one is in the sea, and one is in the earth.

artifacts.name: Andúril
artifacts.description: The reforged sword of Elendil, Narsil. Borne by Aragorn as symbol of his kingship. Flame of the West.

artifacts.name: Sting
artifacts.description: A dagger forged in Gondolin that glows blue when Orcs are near. Borne by Bilbo and Frodo.

artifacts.name: Glamdring
artifacts.description: The Foe-hammer, sword of Elrond, later borne by Gandalf. Forged in Gondolin.

artifacts.name: The Mithril Coat
artifacts.description: A mail shirt of mithril, lighter than silk but stronger than tempered steel. Given to Frodo by Bilbo.
